items.title: Require typing_extensions on Python < 3.13
items.body:
On newer Python releases, the typing module has all we need.

Fixes: #189

items.title: Add configuration source from environment variables
items.body:
This PR adds a new `ConfigSource` subclass called `EnvSource` that pulls configuration from environment variables. This allows an application using `confuse` to have a layered configuration based on YAML files, command-line args, and environment variables. To avoid potentially breaking changes, there is no `EnvSource` loaded by default when creating a `Configuration` object. I think that could be a useful feature for a future version, but for now, applications would need to manually opt-in to environment based configs, and they can choose whether to place it above or below command-line configs in precedence.

To help implement `EnvSource`, the `ConfigView._build_namespace_dict` function was refactored into the utility function `util.build_dict`. In addition, this new utility function gained an option for how to handle `None` values. Originally, `None` values were always dropped, which is necessary when processing command-line arg `Namespaces` that populate keys with `None` values when args are missing. However, for environment variables, which don't have defaults when not present, I think keeping `None` values is desirable to allow config options to be "unset" using an environment variable.

To make `EnvSource` configs compatible with YAML-based configs, the values of environment variables are parsed using a YAML `Loader` class (confuse's own `yaml_util.Loader` by default). This ensures consistent type conversion between YAML files and environment variables. For example, the string "1.0" becomes a `float`, and "true" becomes `True`. By default, environment variables are forced to be parsed as scalars, but there is an option (`parse_yaml_docs`) that parses the variable's value as a full YAML doc. This would allow, for example, nested dicts to be set in single environment variable and could be useful for very deep configuration structures. However, since this might be more than most applications would want, full YAML parsing is disabled by default.

These are the other features of the `EnvSource` configuration source:
- A `prefix` is required so that only environment variables with the given prefix will be included in the config. The `prefix` is stripped from the variable name before setting the key for the config.
- Nested configurations are supported using the `sep` parameter, which defaults to double underscore. Double underscore was chosen as the default so that there would not be clashes with configurations that already use single underscores in keys and because environment variable names must be alphanumeric or underscore under BASH (ie, cannot use dots), but applications are free to use any separator string that they want when initializing an `EnvSource`.
- By default, variable names are converted to lowercase before becoming keys in the configuration source, but this can be disabled by setting `lower` to `False` when initializing an `EnvSource`.
- Because configurations may include lists but lists are not directly supported by the "nested dict" approach with a separator string, a method to convert "list-like" dicts to true lists is included and enabled by default. Basically, a dict of the form `{0: 'a', 1: 'b', 2: 'c'}` is converted to the list `['a', 'b', 'c']`. This allows environment variables of the form `[PREFIX][TOP-LEVEL KEY]__[INDEX]` to be used for lists. Nested lists and lists at any level of the configuration (except for the top level) are supported. This default list behavior can be disabled by setting `handle_lists` to `False` when initializing an `EnvSource`.

No documentation is included in this initial PR, but I'm happy to add documentation if this `EnvSource` configuration source seems useful and once the implementation/behavior is finalized.

items.title: Add options for Filename templates to resolve relative paths using source file location
items.body:
These two commits allow confuse ConfigSources and Filename templates to be set up to resolve relative paths from the base directory of the configuration file itself, rather than the application's configuration directory. The new behavior is opt-in.

The first commit implements the new relative path behavior at the ConfigSource level, by allowing the source file to be marked as resolving paths relative to its base directory. This was the suggested approach in response to #125.

The second commit provides an additional way to invoke the new relative path behavior at the level of an individual template, regardless of the setting for the source. This could potentially allow applications to have more fine-grained control over path resolution. It would also allow applications to resolve paths in the application's default `config_default.yaml` file relative to that location within the package. This could be useful for packages with default settings that refer to a default data file. However, if it is not desirable to have two ways to invoke the same behavior, the second commit could be dropped.

items.title: Add helper to interpret items as key-value pairs (port from confit)
items.body:
This brings the remaining feature from beetbox/beet's confit across to confuse. This feature was originally added for beets' fetchart plugin to support configuration like this:

```yaml
fetchart:
    sources:
        - filesystem
        - coverart: release
        - itunes
        - coverart: releasegroup
        - '*'
```
This is meant to be read as a list of key-value pairs, where the value is optional. The above configuration is read using `default_value='*'` to result in the sequence of pairs:
```python
[
    ('filesystem',  '*'           ),
    ('coverart',    'release'     ),
    ('itunes',      '*'           ),
    ('coverart',    'releasegroup'),
    ('*',           '*'           ),
]
```

items.title: Rename confit to confuse
items.body: Before this package gets widely adopted, it would be a good idea to properly rename 'confit' to 'confuse'. This PR takes care of most of it; you will still need to rename the github repo and the readthedocs project.
